verdicts.note: Refers to herself as 'the only girl'; female throughout.
Confirms mechanical engineering (chose mechanical over automotive); opening turn confirms it.
Loughborough = pre-1992 university; wants to stay there.
Explicitly repeating Part B = Year 2.
Maths/physics favourites; got A's then B's; strong support for being good at maths/science.
Names problem solving as an appeal, hedged; agree fits.
Explicitly 'never looked at it', 'didn't know enough'; strong support for little knowledge.
Chose mechanical for being 'more diverse'/broad over too-focussed automotive; maps to varied appeal.
Careers people suggested engineering; agree defensible despite her initial resistance.
Engineers told her 'don't do engineering'; clear yes.
Names engineers explicitly as those who discouraged her.
Dad 'used to be an engineer' = family member in industry, but she repeatedly says she didn't know about engineering; thin, downgrade confidence.
Parents supported whatever she chose, not engineering specifically; neutral is apt.
Intends to go on placement; has applied and interviewed.
Names experience as the primary reason, reiterated; strongly agree fits.
Cites money as a key gain/reason ('partly for the money').
Decided partly because friend without placement struggles to get a job; maps to improving job chances.
'experience in the working atmosphere' maps to seeing what industry is really like.
'depends how the year out goes... if it inspires me I'll stay' = placement to help decide future direction.
'creditation on my degree' = credibility/standing, not improving GRADES on return; item is specifically about grades. Not supported.
Affirms 'I think so' to applying uni learning, though interviewer-prompted and heavily hedged; thin but already low confidence.
Placement is an optional sandwich choice (not compulsory); additional reasons personal -> 'other'.
Item is a reason for NOT going; she intends to go and was rejected from 2 but still pursuing. Quote does not support this reason-for-not-going item.
Ideal career = designing cars (design work), though she disclaims it; design work is the named preference.
Assigned quote ('group work quite good') only weakly implies skill development; real support ('communication skills... if 2nd year, yes') is interviewer-prompted and qualified. Downgrade.
'quite good... mostly good groups' = satisfied.
'really good tutor' supports very satisfied with personal tutor.
Worst = hard-to-understand lecturers but some good ones; mixed -> neutral is defensible.
'the one is enough' implies current level roughly adequate; conservative neutral acceptable, confidence already low.
'doesn't seem like engineering... or worthwhile' = difficulty seeing relevance; agree well supported.

Quote is a joke about competition for her if more women join; elsewhere refers to the INDUSTRY being competitive. Neither supports 'engineering STUDENTS are competitive'. Reasoning itself admits weak support.
